messages:
anna_ops: FYI rolling edge-prefetch route change to eu-west now. Canary showed OK but seeing a tiny cluster of 502s from real traffic. Looks like a subset of edge nodes still answering via old route because of prefetch + DNS TTL. Can we page oncall? :warning:

sre-bot: INCIDENT | paging oncall for channel incidents — high error spike in eu-west (502s) detected by edge-metrics probe

deploy-bot: Deploy started: edge-prefetch-route-v5 -> eu-west (canary 10%) at 15:23 UTC

mike_oncall: On it. Paging in. @anna_ops — how widespread? any customer reports?

anna_ops: Appears partial: ~8% of requests to eu-west seeing 502s and higher latency. Customer tickets trickling in (tariq_support linked). Most e2e checks pass for new route, but old route still resolves from some edges due to prefetch cache + long CNAME TTL we set during rollout.

jess_platform: Can you paste the DNS outputs and an example curl?

anna_ops: Sure — snippets:```
; dig new route
;; ANSWER SECTION:
edge-prefetch.example.com. 3600 IN CNAME edge-eu-v5.example.net.
edge-eu-v5.example.net. 3600 IN A 54.12.34.56

; dig old route seen from one problematic node
;; ANSWER SECTION:
edge-prefetch.example.com. 86400 IN CNAME edge-eu-v4.example.net.
edge-eu-v4.example.net. 86400 IN A 52.98.76.54

# curl traces from two requests (one good, one bad)
curl -s -D - https://api.example.com/health -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{remote_ip}\n"
200 54.12.34.56
502 52.98.76.54
```

tariq_support: Got ~12 tickets referencing 502 in EU-SUB region, mostly between 15:24-15:27 UTC. Customers A, C reported transient errors, retried OK. Adding ticket refs: AP-12345, AP-12346

mike_oncall: Ok. Two parallel actions: 1) flip kill-switch (feature flag) to disable prefetch route change, 2) try to nudge DNS/edge prefetch cache where possible. Which is lower risk?

jess_platform: Kill-switch first. We have feature flag `edge_prefetch_routing.v5` — set to false will force fallback to v4. Command:```
# flagsvc set edge_prefetch_routing.v5 false --env=prod --scope=eu-west
flagsvc: success — edge_prefetch_routing.v5=false
```

deploy-bot: Feature flag change applied by jess_platform at 15:29 UTC — edge_prefetch_routing.v5=false

mike_oncall: I triggered flag. Monitoring...

anna_ops: Seeing immediate drop in 502s from the subset that hit the old A record. Overall 502 rate down from 8% -> 0.6% in 30s. Latency normalizing.

jess_platform: For remediation, we should also flush prefetch caches on affected edge nodes (there's a known issue where prefetch cache will keep the older CNAME until TTL expiry even if flag flips). Runbook snippet:```
# run on edge pool eu-west-prefetch-*
kubectl exec -n edge $(kubectl get pods -l app=edge-prefetch -o name | head -n 1) -- /bin/sh -c \"curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/cache/flush\"
```

anna_ops: Kicking cache flush to 6 nodes now.

sre-bot: NOTE | cache-flush jobs started (6 nodes) by anna_ops

customer-alerts: Status update: affected customers experiencing transient errors; mitigated by flag rollback. Not a data-loss event. Severity lowered to P2. We will notify impacted customers with ETA for follow-up.

mike_oncall: Good. Root cause hypothesis: we shortened rollout but forgot that some edge nodes had long CNAME TTLs and aggressive prefetch. The combination allowed a subset to keep pointing at v4 while the rest moved to v5 -> routing divergence and 502s. Flag rollback + cache flush is stopgap.

tariq_support: Sending customer PM updates now: short apology + note that we rolled back change and investigating.

jess_platform: Followups I want on the ticket: 1) Adjust rollout tooling to check for CNAME TTLs and prefetch behavior before switch, 2) add a canary probe that compares resolved CNAMEs across edge pools after route flip, 3) consider lowering the TTL during rollout window or use staged DNS with per-edge overrides.

anna_ops: Agree. Also propose an escaped-route test in CD pipeline that simulates DNS TTL > 1h and prefetch enabled to catch divergence.

mike_oncall: I'll own immediate postmortem with timeline. Action items: @jess_platform create PR for canary probe, @anna_ops write doclet about TTL checks, @sre-bot schedule runbook update. Assigning follow-ups in tracker.

deploy-bot: Rollout aborted at 15:30 UTC and revert completed.

anna_ops: Monitoring shows stable since 15:31. I'll keep an eye for next 30m then close the incident.

mike_oncall: Thanks all. Lessons captured, postmortem scheduled for tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

jess_platform: Quick note — if we re-run, temporarily set CNAME TTL=60s during canary + a probe that checks edge-resolve parity every 10s.

anna_ops: closing loop: no further tickets in last 12m. closing thread after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
